questions.question: How many paths of travel does each traffic lane provide for a motorcyclist?
questions.explanation: Each traffic lane has three paths for motorcyclists: left, center, and right.

questions.question: When following a car, where should you ride in the lane?
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of the lane when following a car. The driver checks the rearview mirror more often than side mirrors. This position makes you more visible.

questions.question: When riding in a group, where should inexperienced riders position themselves?

options.text: At the tail end of the group.

questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride just behind the leader. This allows experienced riders to watch them without making the inexperienced rider lead the group.

questions.question: What is the best group formation when riding through curves, turning, or entering a highway?
questions.explanation: Use a single-file line when riding through curves, making turns, or entering or exiting a highway. Staggered formation is best for straightaways.

questions.question: When riding a three-wheeled motorcycle through a curve, what should you do?

options.text: Stay in the center of the lane.
Stay on the outside of the lane.

questions.explanation: Three-wheeled motorcycles handle curves differently than two-wheeled motorcycles. You may need to move from the outside to the inside of the curve before straightening out.

questions.question: Should you wear a leather jacket when riding in warm weather?

options.text: No, it will make you too hot.
Yes, but take frequent breaks to remove the jacket and cool off.
Yes, riding jackets are designed to keep you cool, even in warm weather.
No, jackets get in the way of steering.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, riding jackets are designed to keep you cool, even in warm weather.
questions.explanation: In warm weather, a riding jacket protects you and helps prevent dehydration. Many jackets are designed to keep riders cool.

questions.question: Which statement is true about motorcycle brakes?

options.text: The front and rear brakes provide equal braking power.
The front brake provides more braking power than the rear brake.
The rear brake provides more braking power than the front brake.
Only use the front brake when braking.

questions.correctAnswerText: The front brake provides more braking power than the rear brake.
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful and provides about 70 percent of your stopping power. Always use both brakes when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: Helmet-wearing riders are how many times more likely to survive a crash?
questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet makes you three times more likely to survive head injuries in a crash than not wearing a helmet.

questions.question: When looking through a turn, what should you do?

options.text: Turn both your head and your shoulders to get a better look.
Turn just your head, not your shoulders.
Only move your eyes, not your head.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn just your head, not your shoulders.
questions.explanation: Look through the turn to where you want to go. Turn your head only, not your shoulders, and keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: How can you reduce your reaction time while riding?

options.text: Ride slower than the speed limit.
Cover the clutch and the brakes.
Pull in the clutch when turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover the clutch and the brakes.
questions.explanation: Cover the clutch and brakes to reduce your reaction time. This helps especially when riding through areas with possible hazards.

questions.question: When braking on a slippery surface, what should you do?

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes.
Press the front brake hard to keep the front tire from locking.
Use either the front or rear brake, but not both at once.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, use both brakes to slow down. Squeeze the front brake lever slowly to avoid locking the front wheel. Use gentle pressure on the rear brake.

questions.question: Proper riding clothes offer all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: Proper clothing protects you from injury in a crash. It also protects you from weather hazards like hot or cold temperatures. Good clothes should be comfortable, not uncomfortable.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, you should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Start slowing down sooner than normal.
Talk to your passenger while riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Talk to your passenger while riding.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight, which makes the motorcycle slower to respond. With a passenger, ride slower, start braking sooner, and leave more space between you and other vehicles. Always tell your passenger about road hazards ahead.

questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, you should not:
questions.explanation: To ride safely on a slippery surface, slow down, avoid sudden movements, and use both brakes gently when you need to stop.

questions.question: If your front wheel begins to skid, you should:

options.text: Keep the front brake on and ride out the skid.
Keep the front brake on and release the rear brake.
Release the front brake right away, then apply it again smoothly.
Release the front brake and press harder on the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake right away, then apply it again smoothly.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks up while braking, release the front brake completely right away. Then apply the brake again smoothly.

questions.question: When riding in a group, what is the best formation?

options.text: A single line, one after another.

questions.explanation: A staggered formation is best for group riding. Switch to a single-file line when turning, going around curves, or entering or leaving a highway.

questions.question: In a group ride, where should inexperienced riders position themselves?

options.text: At the front of the group.
At the back of the group.

questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride right behind the leader. This way they won't get left behind, and experienced riders can watch them from behind.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions or hazards.

questions.question: What is the best lane position for a motorcycle rider?

options.text: The left side of the lane.
The right side of the lane.
There is no single best position for all situations.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is no single best position for all situations.
questions.explanation: The best lane position depends on your current road conditions. Choose a position that keeps you safe, gives you space to move, and makes you visible to other drivers.

questions.question: If a small animal enters your lane while you are riding in traffic, you should:

options.text: Swerve into other lanes if needed to avoid the animal.
Change lanes as fast as you can.
Flash your lights to scare the animal away.

questions.explanation: Do what you safely can to avoid hitting an animal. But if you are in traffic, stay in your lane. Swerving into another lane to avoid a small animal could cause you to hit another vehicle. A small animal is less dangerous than a collision with a car.

questions.question: In hot weather, wearing a riding jacket:

options.text: Can help protect you from heat exhaustion and dehydration.
Is not recommended because it can cause heat-related problems.
Should only be worn if the jacket is light colored.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can help protect you from heat exhaustion and dehydration.
questions.explanation: Wear a riding jacket and long pants even in hot weather. They protect you from injuries and also help prevent heat exhaustion and dehydration.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limits are rectangular with white backgrounds and black lettering. Follow all rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: Usually, a minimum following distance of _____ should be maintained.
questions.explanation: Keep at least two seconds of distance between you and the vehicle ahead. Increase this to three seconds or more in bad weather or poor riding conditions.

questions.question: When riding, you should:

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look through turns.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn only your head and eyes to look where you are going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head and eyes to look where you are going.
questions.explanation: When turning, look ahead by turning only your head and eyes. Keep your knees against the gas tank for balance. Keep your arms slightly bent when holding the handgrips.

questions.question: A person who is above the legal drinking age with a blood alcohol content (BAC) of ______ is considered legally intoxicated.
questions.explanation: In Louisiana, a person under 21 is legally intoxicated at 0.02 percent BAC or higher. A person 21 or older is legally intoxicated at 0.08 percent BAC or higher. Never drive or ride while intoxicated—it is illegal and dangerous.
